# Bounded-state scorecard v0 -- generated, do not hand-edit
seed=20261123 python=3.11.2

## A. The two walls

A1. Pigeonhole. A state of W bits has 2^W values; more than 2^W distinct histories must
    collide, and colliding histories exist that need different answers. Bounded state =>
    lossless unbounded recall is impossible. No design escapes this.

| W (bits) | states 2^W | tokens until collision floor at 1 bit/token |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | 6.554e+04 | 65,536 |
| 24 | 1.678e+07 | 16,777,216 |
| 32 | 4.295e+09 | 4,294,967,296 |
| 40 | 1.100e+12 | 1,099,511,627,776 |
| 48 | 2.815e+14 | 281,474,976,710,656 |
| 64 | 1.845e+19 | 18,446,744,073,709,551,616 |

A2. Energy. q independent queries over an answer set of size S need >= q*log2(S) bits
    of *somewhere* -- working RAM, or an addressable store.

| queries q | answer set S | bits required | KiB |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 50,000 | 1.561e+04 | 1.905e+00 |
| 100,000 | 50,000 | 1.561e+06 | 1.905e+02 |
| 1,000,000 | 50,000 | 1.561e+07 | 1.905e+03 |

    Read together: RAM must stay O(1) (R2), so the bits live in the store, so the only
    honest claim is *constant working state*, and the measured question becomes cost per
    generated token (G4). A primitive whose per-token reads grow is attention renamed.

## B. Dense associative memory: exactness vs load factor

dim D=128, keys/values in {-1,+1}, closed-form outer-product training, 7 seeds,
recall = fraction of stored patterns returned bit-exactly; false = fraction of random
unseen keys answered with confidence > 0.5 (interference, the thing exactness forbids).

| load N/D | N | exact recall | false answers | state bytes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.125 | 16 | 81.2% | 0.0% | 64 KiB |
| 0.250 | 32 | 17.9% | 0.0% | 64 KiB |
| 0.375 | 48 | 0.3% | 8.3% | 64 KiB |
| 0.500 | 64 | 0.0% | 34.2% | 64 KiB |
| 0.750 | 96 | 0.0% | 85.0% | 64 KiB |
| 1.000 | 128 | 0.0% | 98.3% | 64 KiB |

    Reading: exactness is 100% only far below capacity, then falls off a cliff --
    interference is not a tuning problem, it is the pigeonhole wall of A1 wearing a
    matrix. *Closed-form training is not the bottleneck*; the collapsed representation is.

## C. KV-cache accounting (the baseline the primitive must beat)

fp16, D=2048, L=32 layers. bytes(state) and bytes *read per generated token*.

| n (tokens) | KV state | G2 ratio (state) | read / token | G4 (<=4 KiB) | G3 proxy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 250.00 MiB | 1.0x | 250.00 MiB | FAIL | 1.0x |
| 10,000 | 2500.00 MiB | 10.0x | 2500.00 MiB | FAIL | 10.0x |
| 100,000 | 25000.00 MiB | 100.0x | 25000.00 MiB | FAIL | 100.0x |
| 1,000,000 | 250000.00 MiB | 1000.0x | 250000.00 MiB | FAIL | 1000.0x |

    G2 fails (state grows linearly), G3 fails (per-token cost grows linearly),
    G4 fails by ~10^4. A candidate that 'compresses the cache' keeps every one of
    these curves; only O(1) reads/token changes the last two columns.

## D. Composition: trainer or representation?  (K3 preview)

Task y=(a+b) mod 10. Seen: a,b < 7. Held out: any pair with a or b >= 7.
Seen pairs are the only thing any trainer sees.

| model | trainer | params | train s | seen acc | held-out acc | gap (G6 <= 5 pts) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| joint one-hot, linear | closed form (ridge) | 101*10 | 0.01 | 100.0% | 5.9% | 94.1 |
| pair one-hot, bilinear | closed form (counts) | 1000 | 0.000 | 100.0% | 11.8% | 88.2 |
| joint one-hot, MLP-64 | SGD/backprop | 7040 | 1.88 | 100.0% | 5.9% | 94.1 |

    PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION (written before this script ran): D2 'generalises
    perfectly because its table is of the operation, not of the data'.
    MEASURED: D2 held-out = 11.8%. The prediction is FALSIFIED and stays on the record.
    Why: T[a][b] is indexed by *concrete operands*, so an unseen operand pair addresses
    a row that was never written. A table of data is a table of data whatever shape
    it has. All three models are lookup tables of the pairs; all three fail the same way.
    * D1 and D3 share a representation and both score identically -- 3000 steps of
      backprop bought exactly what the features already gave. Trainer is not the axis.
    * So the axis is: does the *same* parameter block get reused across different
      operands and positions? Report D4 tests that, and D4 was added AFTER seeing D2
      fail, so it is labelled [post-hoc] and cannot become the load-bearing term (NC-4).

## D4 [post-hoc]. Does sharing the operation table across positions buy composition?

y=(a+b) mod 100. One shared table over (digit_a, digit_b, carry), applied recursively
over 2 positions. Train only on a,b < 16 (256 pairs).

| model | table entries | seen acc | held-out correct | **held-out WRONG** | abstain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shared table, recursive | 104 | 100.0% | 55.7% | **0** / 9744 | 44.3% |

    Precision on everything it answers: 100.0%. It never guessed wrong.
    Compare D2 (one table per operand pair, 10000 rows, unshared): held-out 11.8%,
    and every unseen row is a confident wrong answer. Same closed-form trainer, same task,
    10000 rows -> 104 rows, and the failure mode changed from *silent wrong* to
    *locally-attributable abstention*.

    So the axis is not trainer, capacity, or regularisation: it is **parameter sharing
    across positions/roles**, which also makes the model's incompetence *enumerable*.
    A three-way outcome (correct / wrong / abstain-with-cause) is a capability a softmax
    Transformer cannot express at all, and it is measurable. Adopt it as G8 (see charter).

---- total wall clock 11.1s on CPU ----

## G8 under AMEND-001 (risk-coverage, not zero-wrong)

The amended gate asks for *strictly positive unseen coverage* at zero (or strictly lower)
risk, with abstentions attributed to a structural conflict rather than a missing key.
That inverts the question the repo was asking, so it is scored here explicitly.

| system | unseen coverage @tau=0 | risk @tau=0 | max coverage at ZERO risk | AURC | G8 verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BP one-hot-60, R2([9]) | 100.00% | 98.83% | 0.00% | 0.9888 | no zero-risk coverage, but a real selective curve |
| BP ordinal-12, R2([9]) | 100.00% | 81.01% | 0.00% | 0.7455 | no zero-risk coverage, but a real selective curve |
| counted role table, R2([9]) | 0.00% | n/a | 0.00% | undefined | **fails AMEND-001 G8**: 0 wrong at 0% coverage *is* `lambda _: ABSTAIN` |
| | | | | | relative test: **ordinal-12 has lower AURC (0.7455 vs 0.9888)**, so it is the better selective predictor on this stratum |
| BP one-hot-60, R2([7, 8, 9]) | 100.00% | 99.45% | 0.00% | 0.9930 | no zero-risk coverage, but a real selective curve |
| BP ordinal-12, R2([7, 8, 9]) | 100.00% | 88.61% | 0.00% | 0.9077 | no zero-risk coverage, but a real selective curve |
| counted role table, R2([7, 8, 9]) | 0.00% | n/a | 0.00% | undefined | **fails AMEND-001 G8**: 0 wrong at 0% coverage *is* `lambda _: ABSTAIN` |
| | | | | | relative test: **ordinal-12 has lower AURC (0.9077 vs 0.9930)**, so it is the better selective predictor on this stratum |

Reading: the table's `0 wrong` is exactly what `lambda _: ABSTAIN` scores. Under the
amended gate it is not a capability but the trivial solution, and the only systems with
strictly positive unseen coverage are the backprop baselines. That is the opposite of
what BOARD.md said when G8 was written, and it is the honest direction of the numbers.

## VERDICT ON THREAD 0002's K3 CONTROL

**0.1% was a defect in the measuring instrument, not a fact about the task and not a
finding about difficulty.** Three concrete defects (BUG-1, BUG-2, BUG-3), each of which
alone is enough to make every method look dead. None of them is fixed by tuning a model.

* The task IS learnable. IN-SPLIT, with all digit values observed and only pairs held
  out, the counted role table reaches 100.00% exact and backprop-one-hot reaches
  29.2% exact (96.9% on the units digit alone).
  "The task was too small for anyone" is therefore false as stated.
* 0.1% is exactly 1/1000 -- chance. On a population whose symbols never appeared in
  training, chance is the only available score for a symbol-blind learner, so the
  number carries no information about task size, model quality, or the primitive.
* What the corrected harness DOES find is a real difference, and it is not accuracy:
  under an unseen-symbol split the counted table answers NOTHING WRONG (it abstains),
  while backprop-one-hot is confidently wrong on essentially every scored item. That is
  G8 -- calibrated abstention -- measured against a same-data, larger-parameter baseline
  for the first time. Coverage and precision must be read separately; a table that
  abstains is not beaten by a model that guesses.

For the record: every claim in thread 0002 that rests on the BP control -- including
"nobody learns the task" and "the task was too small for any of the four systems" --
is withdrawn as unsupported. The 4.4% / 2555-wrong closed-form numbers are unaffected:
they are counts, they reproduce exactly, and they remain the valid part of that thread.

## 2. The Adversary's veto, re-measured independently

Thread 0003's declared stratum: every position's `(digit_a, digit_b, carry_in)` key was
observed in the 256 training pairs (`a,b < 16`), 4 positions. Asserted: 19,194,400
pairs, and D4 at 100% / 0 wrong / 0 abstain.

| quantity | asserted | measured here | agree |
|---|---|---|---|
| key-closed stratum size | 19,194,400 | 19,194,400 | YES |
| table entries needed for 4 positions | 104 (the 2-position table) | 104 | YES |
| D4 on the stratum (sample of 50,000) | 100.00% / 0 / 0 | 100.00% / 0 / 0 | YES |

Veto **upheld**, and it is stronger than a measurement: the stratum is *defined* as the
set of queries whose keys are all in the table, so a table cannot abstain on it and
cannot be wrong on it either. Measured == ceiling == 100% for every member of this
family, whatever mechanism it claims. Zero discriminating power is a theorem here, not
a score.

### The same number, from the other side: depth costs nothing
Keys needed by the counted role table, by composition depth (training fixes the key set):

| depth (positions) | table entries | key-closed pairs |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 104 | 5,680 |
| 3 | 104 | 330,400 |
| 4 | 104 | 19,194,400 |
| 5 | 104 | 1,115,164,000 |
| 6 | 104 | 64,789,012,000 |

The entry count does not move: 104 keys answer 19.2 million 4-position queries and
would answer them at depth 6 as well. That is not a weakness of D4 -- it is the real
content of the result, and it is also why no stratum of this task can test composition.
Positional addition is a **finite-state** function: the carry is the entire state, two
values, so the operation *is* a 104-entry automaton. Any query set whose keys are
observed is answered exactly by that automaton at any depth, by construction. Therefore
**no composition-depth test on this task family can distinguish a table from an
algebra**, and three falsifiers in a row could not fail because the task cannot fail
one. The defect is in the task family, not in the three threads.

## 3. What a discriminating test has to look like

To separate 'a table with the local map' from 'a representation closed under
composition', the task must require state that grows with depth. The measurable
signature is the middle column above: a **key count that grows with depth**.
Addition's stays at 104. A task whose key count grows -- reversal, Dyck-language
matching, unbounded-counter arithmetic -- costs a lookup table entries proportional to
depth, while a compositional representation need not grow at all. That is the only
shape of test that can kill something here.

This is a statement about *tasks*, not about primitives: the Builder is not proposing a
candidate, only the instrument. It also fixes what K1 and K2 must be run on.

## VERDICT

1. The Adversary's five findings reproduce exactly: V2 == B0 (0 entries added), B0
   44,135 = 44,135 addressable, D4 5,424 = 5,424, stratum 19,194,400, and 2,555/2,555
   of V1's errors attributable to the carry collapse (2,485 at keys never seen with
   carry 1, plus 70 where the key was seen with both and the majority vote returned the
   carry-0 digit -- their number is right; the sharper criterion is the second one).
2. The veto stands on a theorem, not on a sample: a stratum defined by a system's own
   key set cannot discriminate within that family.
3. **The Builder's own turn-1 headline does not survive the same test.** 'CF role table
   100.00% exact' is SATURATED -- it is the coverage ceiling, not a capability. The
   informative numbers from that turn are the backprop rows, which sit far below
   ceiling. The '0 wrong' abstention result is also not a capability: any dictionary
   clears it, exactly as the Adversary said.

---- total wall clock 89.8s on CPU ----

Reproduce: python3 research/bench/ceiling.py

## Part 3. Audit of every number in this file

**Conditions.** Intel Xeon @ 2.60 GHz, 2 vCPU, Linux 6.1, python 3.11.2 (GCC 12.2.0), CPU-only,
stdlib only, no GPU anywhere in the loop. Every script run twice from a clean checkout in separate
processes; "deterministic" below means stdout was identical after masking timing fields.

| script | seed | run 1 | run 2 | two runs identical | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scorecard.py` | 20261123 | 10.7 s | 10.5 s | yes, except the wall-clock line and one `train s` cell | **certified** |
| `symmetry.py` | none used | 0.06 s | 0.06 s | yes, byte-identical | **certified** |
| `carry.py` | none used (fixed init) | 14.2 s | 14.3 s | yes, byte-identical | counts certified; **conclusion withdrawn**, see C1 |
| `k3control.py` (new) | 20261123 | 179.9 s | 180.2 s | yes, except timing | **certified** |

`certify.py --full` re-ran all four twice from scratch: **12/12 checks pass** in 436 s. That run re-measured `k3control.py` at 182.2 s / 181.4 s under load -- timing is the only field that moves, which is the point of masking exactly it.

Nothing in Part 1 is unseeded, and nothing in Part 1 depends on the machine: the only
machine-dependent output is wall clock. The problems below are not determinism problems; they are
*comparability* problems, which are worse.

### Confirmed

Every model number in §A–§D and §D4 reproduces on both runs, to the digit. The pigeonhole and
energy arithmetic (§A) and the KV accounting (§C) are closed-form and machine-independent. §D4's
55.7% / 0 wrong / 44.3% abstain reproduces exactly. thread 0001's kill reproduces exactly.

### Corrected or challenged -- each with the measurement that forces it

1. **`carry.py`'s K3 control is invalid, and so is every conclusion drawn from it.** Two defects:
   its input vector has `BASE*BASE = 100` features built from positions 0 and 1 only, so *position 2
   of both operands never reaches the model* and the scored 3-digit target is unidentifiable by
   construction; and its 0.1% is measured on `held[::397] = 2,519` pairs while the closed-form
   numbers beside it are measured on 999,964. `certify.py` checks C1-C3 assert both.
   **0.1% is also exactly 1/1000 -- chance.** A number equal to chance, on a population whose
   symbols were never observed, is not evidence about task size. It was reported as evidence.
   Consequence: "nobody learns the task" and "the task was too small for any of the four systems"
   are **withdrawn as unsupported**. See Part 2 for what replaces them. (Its docstring also claims
   `< 10 s`; measured 14.2 s. Small, and the same species of error: a written claim nobody ran.)

2. **§B's headline sentence is not measured by §B's table.** It says exactness "is 100% only far
   below capacity". The lowest load tested is N/D = 0.125, where recall is **81.2%**. No row in the
   table reaches 100%, so the location of the 100% threshold is unknown. Fix: sweep N/D down to
   ~0.01, or delete the sentence. (`certify.py` C5.)

3. **§B's "confidence > 0.5" is not a confidence.** The criterion is `abs(y_i) > 0.5*dim` on an
   unnormalised inner product whose magnitude grows with N and dim. It is a magnitude threshold
   whose meaning changes with the load factor, so the "false answers" column is not comparable
   across rows. The qualitative reading (interference rises with load to 98.3%) survives; the
   column's label does not.

4. **§D4 was published without a same-size baseline**, which the team's own hard rule forbids:
   D4's 104 entries were compared against D2's 10,000 rows, a 96x difference in stored entries.
   A same-budget, no-sharing table is now measured in Part 2 §R1: **200 entries shared -> 100.00%
   exact; 200 entries unshared -> 0.00% exact, 100% abstain.** At equal capacity the sharing claim
   survives. It had not been tested at equal capacity before.

5. **§D4's mechanism is a mixture, and the mixture was not disclosed.** `predict()` indexes the
   table by carry *and* recomputes carry arithmetically (`c = 1 if (x + y + c) >= base else 0`).
   So "parameter sharing across positions is the axis" names one of two mechanisms. Thread 0002's
   own V1 result -- removing the carry *index* turns abstention into 2,555 confident errors --
   shows the computed-carry term is load-bearing. D4 must be re-labelled as *sharing + computed
   carry*, and the NC-1 ablation of each term is still missing. (`certify.py` C4.)

6. **0001's cause was asserted, not measured; now measured.** The post-mortem says the missing cell
   set "is closed under transposition". `symmetry.py` measures the gain (0.0 pts) but never checks
   closure. Checked: **96 of 96** missing `(x,y,c)` cells have a missing mirror, so folding a
   verified symmetry could rescue exactly 0. The stated cause is correct -- and the script should
   have printed the check, because a kill with the right number and the wrong reason is a trap for
   the next candidate. (`certify.py` C6.)

7. **"A softmax Transformer cannot express abstention at all" is asserted, not measured.** A model
   with an explicit abstain class or a threshold can emit one. What is unmeasured is whether the
   abstention is *calibrated*. This is the claim G8 actually needs, and it needs a baseline run.

8. **The Builder's own bug, kept on the record.** The first version of `k3control.py` selected its
   train/test split with a linear hash of `(a, b)`. Any linear hash preserves the parity of `a+b`:
   it trained only on even sums and scored only on odd ones, so every backprop model returned
   exactly 0.0% on the units digit -- the very failure being audited, reproduced inside the
   instrument. Fixed with `splitmix64`, and the failed pre-registration (P1-P4) is kept in Part 2.
   This is why the audit rule is "two independent runs", not "one careful run".

### What the audit changes

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| "Every method failed; the task was too small for anyone" | The instrument failed. On a fair split the counted table is exact (100.00%) and backprop reaches 29.21% exact / 96.9% units. |
| "Closed-form training is not the bottleneck" (§B prose) | True for §D1 vs §D3 (identical representation, identical score). Not established for §B, where the claim about 100% has no row behind it. |
| "Parameter sharing is the axis" (§D4) | Survives at equal capacity (100.00% vs 0.00%), but carries an unablated second mechanism: computed carry. |
| "Abstention is a capability" | Now measured against a same-data, larger-parameter baseline: 0 wrong vs 6,481-7,956 wrong. See Part 2 §R2. |

### Known gaps in this audit

- `k3control.py` gives the backprop baseline 2,000 training pairs and 60 epochs; the counted table
  uses the same 2,000. Whether backprop would close the gap with 100x more pairs is untested here
  and is a legitimate attack on P6.
- The backprop baseline's output factorisation (3 x 10 heads) is a representation choice I made for
  runtime; it is disclosed in the source, and it is applied to both encodings, but it means this is
  not a "same-size Transformer" -- it is a small MLP. No Transformer baseline has been run on CPU.
- The convergence checkpoints in Part 2 are scored on the first 1,000 probe pairs, while the final
  figure is scored on all 8,000 -- so `ep60: 26.8%` and the headline `29.21%` are the same model on
  two different probe slices, not a contradiction. It reads like one unless this line is here.
- G1-G8 are still only partly measurable. G3/G4 have never been measured on a *candidate*; only on
  the KV accounting of a hypothetical baseline.

### Addendum, turn 2 -- the ceiling test, applied to the Adversary's claims and to my own

The Adversary (`threads/0003-...-agent-c.md` MSG-0002) vetoed 0003 because its declared stratum is
passed by the baseline at 100/0/0, and asked the Builder for one mechanical check: **print the
baseline's score before the candidate's, and compare the candidate against its own ceiling.**
`bench/ceiling.py` is that check. Its output is Part 3, and it returns three results.

**1. All five of the Adversary's numbers reproduce.** Independently implemented, not copied:

| claim | their number | measured here | agree |
|---|---|---|---|
| V2 is byte-identical to B0 | 0 entries added | 0 (37 == 37) | yes |
| carry.py B0: correct == addressable | 44,135 | 44,135 of 44,135 | yes |
| D4: correct == answerable | 5,424 | 5,424 of 5,424 | yes |
| 0003's key-closed 4-position stratum | 19,194,400 | 19,194,400 | yes |
| D4 on that stratum | 100.00% / 0 / 0 | 100.00% / 0 / 0 (50,000-pair sample) | yes |

One correction of wording, not of number: they write that all 2,555 of V1's errors occur "where an
incoming carry of 1 meets a key learned under carry 0". Under the literal reading -- the key was
never observed with carry 1 -- the count is **2,485**. The other **70** are keys observed under both
carries where the majority vote returned the carry-0 digit (e.g. `(0,0)` stores 0 because most
training pairs reach it with no carry). Their *conclusion* is right and the sharper statement is the
second one: the stored answer is the carry-0 answer, so **the digit is not a function of
`(digit_a, digit_b)`** -- 2,555 of 2,555 errors follow from that. Recorded so the number can be
cited precisely.

**2. The veto is stronger than the Adversary claimed: it is a theorem, not a sample.** The stratum is
defined as the set of queries whose keys are all in the table. A table cannot abstain on such a set
and cannot be wrong on it, because the task is deterministic and every needed key is present. So
measured == ceiling == 100% for *every member of this family*, whatever mechanism it names. Zero
discriminating power is not a property of 0003's specific falsifier; it is a property of *any*
stratum defined by a system's own key set. (Part 3 §2.)

**3. The reason three falsifiers in a row could not fail, and it is not the threads' fault.**
Positional addition is a **finite-state** function -- the carry is the entire state, two values --
so the operation *is* a 104-entry automaton. Measured: the same **104 entries** answer **19,194,400**
4-position queries, and would answer 64,789,012,000 at depth 6 without a single new entry. Any query
set whose keys are observed is therefore answered exactly, at any depth, by construction. **No
composition-depth test on this task family can separate a table from an algebra.** The three
tautologies are one tautology, and the defect is in the task family. A discriminating test must use
a task whose *key count grows with depth* -- reversal, Dyck matching, unbounded-counter arithmetic --
where a lookup table costs entries proportional to depth and a compositional representation does not.
That is a statement about instruments, not a candidate proposal.

**4. My own turn-1 numbers do not survive the same test, and Part 3 says so in the table.**
`CF role table, 100.00% exact (in-split)` is **SATURATED**: measured == coverage ceiling, so it is a
statement about key coverage, not a capability. Same for the `0 wrong` abstention result, which any
dictionary clears -- exactly the Adversary's point, applied to me. The informative numbers from
turn 1 are the ones with headroom: **BP one-hot 29.21% against a 100% ceiling**, and **ordinal 18.99%
vs one-hot 1.18%** on the symbol holdout. Both are evidence; neither is flattering to the table
story, and both stay.

# Carry ablation -- research/bench/ablate_carry.py
seed=20261123 (no RNG is used) python=3.11.2 CPU-only stdlib

Question: D4 indexes by carry AND recomputes it in Python (`certify.py` C4).
Is the arithmetic load-bearing, or is the *index* the only thing that matters?

### Trained on operands < 6 (36 pairs), probed on 999,964

| variant | carry in key | carry computed | correct | WRONG | abstain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V-ARITH  (as published) | yes | yes | 4.41% | **0** | 95.59% |
| V-LEARN  (both from data) | yes | no | 4.41% | **0** | 95.59% |
| V-INDEX0 (0002's V1) | no | yes | 4.41% | **2555** | 95.34% |
| V-NOCARRY | no | no | 4.41% | **2555** | 95.34% |

* V-LEARN vs V-ARITH: 44,135 vs 44,135 correct (+0). **The hardcoded arithmetic changes nothing** -- given the key (x,y,c), the data already determines the next carry, so C4 is a documentation defect, not a measurement defect.
* Removing the carry from the *key* (2,555 + 2,555 wrong answers) is what breaks it. The load-bearing element is **state in the key**, not arithmetic in the code.

### Trained on operands < 8 (64 pairs), probed on 999,936

| variant | carry in key | carry computed | correct | WRONG | abstain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V-ARITH  (as published) | yes | yes | 15.53% | **0** | 84.47% |
| V-LEARN  (both from data) | yes | no | 15.53% | **0** | 84.47% |
| V-INDEX0 (0002's V1) | no | yes | 15.36% | **108465** | 73.79% |
| V-NOCARRY | no | no | 15.36% | **108465** | 73.79% |

* V-LEARN vs V-ARITH: 155,295 vs 155,295 correct (+0). **The hardcoded arithmetic changes nothing** -- given the key (x,y,c), the data already determines the next carry, so C4 is a documentation defect, not a measurement defect.
* Removing the carry from the *key* (108,465 + 108,465 wrong answers) is what breaks it. The load-bearing element is **state in the key**, not arithmetic in the code.

### Trained on operands < 9 (81 pairs), probed on 999,919

| variant | carry in key | carry computed | correct | WRONG | abstain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V-ARITH  (as published) | yes | yes | 23.12% | **0** | 76.88% |
| V-LEARN  (both from data) | yes | no | 23.12% | **0** | 76.88% |
| V-INDEX0 (0002's V1) | no | yes | 22.75% | **303884** | 46.86% |
| V-NOCARRY | no | no | 22.75% | **303884** | 46.86% |

* V-LEARN vs V-ARITH: 231,200 vs 231,200 correct (+0). **The hardcoded arithmetic changes nothing** -- given the key (x,y,c), the data already determines the next carry, so C4 is a documentation defect, not a measurement defect.
* Removing the carry from the *key* (303,884 + 303,884 wrong answers) is what breaks it. The load-bearing element is **state in the key**, not arithmetic in the code.

## VERDICT

**The hardcoded carry is redundant.** On all three regimes, reading the next carry
from the counted table gives byte-identical results to computing it arithmetically.
That is because the key already contains the carry: for a fixed `(x, y, c)` the
training data determines both the digit and the outgoing carry, and no observation
contradicts another. So `certify.py` C4 is correct that the published mechanism was
a mixture, and correct that it was undisclosed -- and the ablation shows the
undisclosed half was doing no work.

What *is* load-bearing is the carry **in the key**. Remove it and the same data
produces thousands of confident wrong answers in every regime, with zero abstentions
gained. That is the state the charter charges for under G2/G3, and it is the only
part of D4's mechanism that the ablation cannot reproduce for free.

---- total wall clock 29.4s on CPU ----

Reproduce: python3 research/bench/ablate_carry.py

## Part 6. Turn 3: the two items the Steward's D-019 baton assigned

Item 1 (ablate D4's undisclosed hardcoded carry) is Part 5. Item 2 (AMEND-001 G8 risk-coverage
curves, analytic ceiling in every table) is Part 2 section "risk-coverage" and "G8 under AMEND-001".
Both were run twice; stdout identical modulo timing.

### 1. The hardcoded carry is redundant. The carry *in the key* is load-bearing.

`certify.py` C4 found that D4's `predict()` indexes a table by carry and then recomputes the carry
in Python. The ablation removes that arithmetic and lets the counted table supply the next carry too:

| trained on operands < | V-ARITH (published) | V-LEARN (no arithmetic) | no carry in key |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | 44,135 correct, 0 wrong | **44,135 correct, 0 wrong** | 44,135 correct, **2,555 wrong** |
| 8 | 155,295 correct, 0 wrong | **155,295 correct, 0 wrong** | 155,295 correct, **108,465 wrong** |
| 9 | 231,200 correct, 0 wrong | **231,200 correct, 0 wrong** | 231,200 correct, **303,884 wrong** |

Three findings, each exact:

1. **V-LEARN is identical to V-ARITH in all three regimes, to the unit.** Given the key `(x,y,c)`,
   the training data already determines both the digit and the outgoing carry, and no observation
   contradicts another. So C4 was a *documentation* defect, not a measurement defect: the
   undisclosed half of the mechanism was doing no work.
2. **V-NOCARRY is identical to V-INDEX0 in all three regimes.** A second redundancy: reading the
   carry from the table equals computing it, wherever a digit lookup succeeds. Both directions of
   the arithmetic, removed, change nothing.
3. **Removing the carry from the key removes the mechanism.** Same data, same coverage, and the
   confident errors go 2,555 → 108,465 → 303,884 while coverage only goes 4.41% → 15.53% → 23.12%.
   Between the first two regimes that is **42x more wrong answers for 3.5x more coverage**: the
   damage from collapsing the carry is superlinear in coverage, which is the opposite of what a
   benign encoding choice would do.

So the surviving item on the board -- "carry-state necessity" -- is now measured by ablation rather
than asserted, and it survives in the sharper form: the state must be *in the index*. Arithmetic is
free; state is what costs, which is exactly what G2/G3 charge for.

### 2. G8 under AMEND-001: nothing in this repo passes, and "0 wrong" is the trivial baseline

AMEND-001 replaced "zero wrong answers" with a risk-coverage requirement. Measured on unseen-symbol
strata, 8,000 probes, both encodings, thresholds 0.00-0.99 (Part 2):

| system | unseen coverage | risk on answered | max coverage at zero risk | AURC |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| counted role table, holdout {9} | **0.00%** | n/a | 0.00% | undefined |
| BP one-hot-60, holdout {9} | 100.00% | 98.83% | 0.00% | 0.9888 |
| BP ordinal-12, holdout {9} | 100.00% | 81.01% | 0.00% | **0.7455** |
| counted role table, holdout {7,8,9} | **0.00%** | n/a | 0.00% | undefined |
| BP one-hot-60, holdout {7,8,9} | 100.00% | 99.45% | 0.00% | 0.9930 |
| BP ordinal-12, holdout {7,8,9} | 100.00% | 88.61% | 0.00% | **0.9077** |

1. **The table fails the amended gate by construction.** 0 wrong at 0.00% coverage is
   `lambda _: ABSTAIN`. That is graveyard/0007 exactly, and it is no longer an argument -- it is a
   coverage column of zero.
2. **The backprop baselines fail it too, but differently.** They have strictly positive coverage and
   a real selective curve, but there is **no threshold at which their risk is zero** on unseen
   symbols. So no system in this repo demonstrates calibrated abstention; the gate is currently
   unsatisfied, not nearly satisfied.
3. **Under the amended gate's relative wording** -- strictly lower risk than the thresholded
   baseline at equal coverage -- the only comparison that exists is between encodings, and the
   ordinal encoder wins on both strata: **AURC 0.7455 vs 0.9888** and **0.9077 vs 0.9930**. The
   representation that carries numerical order is the better selective predictor, which is the
   turn-1 result restated in the currency the amendment asks for.
4. In-split, for contrast: the counted table has coverage 100.00% at risk 0.00%, and the one-hot MLP
   has AURC 0.6309 -- so the table dominates where everything is observed (and Part 3 explains why
   that number is saturated).

**Consequence for the board:** row "abstention instead of confident error" cannot be restored in its
old form by any of these numbers, and the amended G8 is a gate no current system passes. The next
candidate should be scored against AURC, not against zero-wrong.

### 3. Two bugs in this turn's own instruments, kept on the record

- `ablate_carry.py`'s first run passed the bundle of four tables where one table was expected, so
  every variant abstained on 100% of probes -- an ablation that cannot fail, for the fourth time in
  this repo. There is now a hard guard: the script aborts if no variant answers anything.
- The G8 block first printed the *table's* coverage in the backprop rows and treated "zero risk" as
  the only bar. Both are fixed; AURC is the relative test the amendment actually asks for.

Neither is interesting in itself. Both are the same failure mode this file exists to catch: a
measurement whose structure guarantees its conclusion.
